data.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Targeting
data.summary: The sample searches the host for cryptocurrency wallet files, browser-extension wallet storage, or private keys, and stages them for exfiltration rather than targeting conventional credentials.
data.description:
Targets are predictable because wallet software uses well-known file and path conventions
— wallet.dat and similar for desktop clients, specific extension storage directories for
browser wallets, and clipboard content matching address-format regular expressions for
opportunistic clipper-style theft. Because a private key or seed phrase gives immediate,
irreversible control of funds with no password reset available, recovery after exposure is
genuinely different from a credential leak: there is no revocation.
data.recommendation:
* Move funds to a new wallet generated on a clean device immediately; a seed phrase or key file exposure cannot be revoked or rotated.
* Identify the specific wallet paths and browser-extension storage the sample targeted to scope which wallets were actually at risk.
* Treat clipboard-matching address theft (see clipboard hijacking) as a related but distinct capability worth checking for separately.
data.short_recommendation: Move funds to a newly generated wallet on a clean device; key and seed exposure cannot be revoked.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Enumerated known wallet file paths and browser-extension storage directories and staged matching files for exfiltration.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Searched fixed wallet-file paths and browser-extension local storage for private-key material.
